blocks.title: Algorithm efficiency
blocks.text: Algorithm efficiency is how well an algorithm uses resources such as time and memory, judged by its time and space complexity.
Bubble Sort is O(n^2): doubling the input makes it take about four times as long. Merge Sort is O(n log n), which grows much more slowly, so it is more efficient for large datasets.

blocks.prompt: Which algorithm is more efficient for large datasets: Bubble Sort, Merge Sort, Selection Sort or Quick Sort (MCQ 5)?
blocks.explanation: (b) Merge Sort, the one the chapter names as efficient for large datasets; Quick Sort (d) is also O(n log n) on average. The question says 'search algorithm' but all options are sorting algorithms.

items: Efficiency: resources used; bubble sort O(n^2) (4 times for double input) versus merge sort O(n log n).
